tts-hotkey-and-badge.note: The toolbar badge is browser UI: CDP cannot screenshot it and this machine has no screen-capture tool (GNOME screenshot D-Bus is denied, no import/xwd/ffmpeg). Badge state is asserted through chrome.action.getBadgeText/getBadgeBackgroundColor/getBadgeTextColor and left as a manual check (a green "TTS" chip on the toolbar icon). Real Ctrl+Shift+Y key presses cannot be dispatched through CDP either — the handler (__humanplayTtsTest.invokeToggle, the exact function chrome.commands.onCommand calls) is invoked instead; pressing the physical shortcut is a manual check.

tts-panel-closed.note: With the side panel closed the extension has no analysis loop (M4 lives in the panel document), so no NEW suggestion can be produced — that is why no automatic speak may appear after the panel closes. What this case proves — the architecture-critical property — is that the speak EXECUTION path (service worker + chrome.tts + the debug record + the badge) is fully independent of the panel document: the SW still tracks the GameState stream, and a speak routed through the production runtime-message path (sent from the content-script isolated world, the only remaining sender with the panel gone) is performed and recorded.
